result.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
result.summary: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories? We tested whether final weights reveal initialization, task order, and earlier trajectory states. Training reorganized the ensemble: initial pairwise distances did not consistently predict final distances. Nevertheless, all 30 trained networks were correctly matched to their initial weights among ten candidates per dataset. Networks sharing an initialization also developed recognizable final hidden representations across different batch schedules, although direct comparisons with initial activity did not recover identity. Learning order remained readable as well. A linear probe decoded the order of two earlier tasks with 100% accuracy on 80 held-out networks after ten epochs of a common final task. Earlier intermediate weight states were partly predictable, but individual initial weights could not be reliably reconstructed. Final weights thus retain selective historical information rather than a complete trajectory record. Perturbed networks recovered classification performance without returning to their unperturbed training paths. This separation persisted across datasets, intervention times, and network layers. Moreover, 2,157 of 2,160 aligned endpoint pairs showed no positive loss barrier at sampled interpolation points, indicating low-loss connections between distinct solutions rather than convergence to one weight vector. Together, these findings show that a shared task constrains networks to related successful solutions without erasing their individual histories. Final weights reflect not only what a network has learned, but also where learning began and how it unfolded.

AI.brief_summary: 研究训练完成后的权重与隐藏表示是否保留学习历史信息：通过初始权重匹配、线性探针解码先前任务顺序、预测早期中间权重状态以及权重插值损失障碍等实验，发现历史痕迹可部分解码但并非完整轨迹记录。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表示中残留可解码历史」的探针式分析思路可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否编码推理轨迹与中间步骤信息，并与轨迹训练、贡献分配的监督方式产生关联，但该研究与视觉多模态推理无直接联系，迁移需较多核查。
